title: request-level kernel cost attribution and lightweight runtime telemetry
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: produce per-request attribution of GPU kernel time and token-cost signals with minimal overhead so we can: (1) correlate tail latency to specific kernel variants, (2) support per-route cost chargebacks for Dedicated customers, and (3) feed weighted signals into the autoscaler. Approach: combine sparse NVTX range annotations at the runtime hotpath with lightweight per-kernel counters emitted as metric samples, and map those to top-level trace spans that align to the request lifecycle (prefill, attention, kv-cache lookup, decode). We will design a compact telemetry envelope (span id, kernel id, bytes_in/bytes_out, tokens_generated, kernel_time_ns, device_id, model_variant) that can be emitted synchronously in-situ for high-impact events and batched for low-priority sampling. The work includes: schema design, implementation in the serving runtime, sampling policy (deterministic + adaptive sampling under high throughput), backpressure-safe emission to the observability pipeline, and dashboards/alerts for regressions. Important trade-offs: instrumentation overhead vs signal fidelity; metric cardinality (per-model-version, per-device) vs storage costs; sensitive data exclusion (no prompt or customer PII in telemetry).
acceptance_criteria: Design doc with telemetry envelope and sampling policy reviewed by Observability and Runtime teams
Prototype implemented: NVTX ranges added to prefill/decode hotpath and per-kernel timers emitted as metrics with <3% median latency overhead in bench harness
Mapping layer in trace collector reconstructs per-request kernel attribution for sampled traces
Dashboard showing per-model and per-variant kernel-time breakdowns, 95th/99th latency attribution, and estimated token-cost per request
Integration test demonstrating backpressure-safe emission (no request failures when metrics pipeline is slow)
progress_updates: 2025-01-16: Kickoff meeting with Observability, Runtime, and Billing teams. Agreed on primary goals and non-goals (we will not include user prompt text in telemetry).
2025-01-22: Prototype NVTX envelope implemented around prefill and decode loops; initial microbench shows ~1.4% median latency increase on p50 for a 16k context model under single-request workloads.
2025-01-30: Benchmarks with small batched workloads revealed higher overhead for synchronous counter writes; switched to per-worker buffered counters flushed on event and on request boundary.
2025-02-04: Design review feedback: Observability asked for stable kernel_id namespace and mapping table; Billing asked for token_count and estimated_cost fields. Updated envelope schema accordingly.

2025-02-10: End-to-end POC: sampled traces reconstruct kernel-attribution for 1% of requests and dashboards render breakdown. Noted high cardinality when including model_variant+device_id; added aggregation guidance in the doc.
